- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–3% per day until reversal signal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish signals (e.g., 0.00, 1.00, 0.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment; align forecast slope with sentiment direction for next 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often lags; add 1–2 day lag correction: shift forecast down by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days post-peak.
